title: Cross-cutting timeline of AI distillation, 2006 to 2026
summary: Knowledge distillation began as an academic model-compression trick (Bucila 2006, Hinton 2015) and spent a decade as a research topic before becoming the default way to build small language models (DistilBERT 2019, Gemma, Llama 3.2, Qwen3). In 2024 it turned into a cloud product line (OpenAI Model Distillation, Amazon Bedrock Model Distillation) and a pricing strategy (Gemini Flash, GPT-4o mini, Haiku). DeepSeek-R1's January 2025 release, with six openly distilled students, triggered a market shock and the first public accusation that a rival had distilled a frontier lab's API outputs. By 2026 distillation was a national-security issue: Anthropic and OpenAI disclosed industrial-scale extraction campaigns, the White House issued a memorandum on adversarial distillation, and Congress introduced the Deterring American AI Model Theft Act and the BLADE Act. This timeline records 90+ dated events across research, product, market, policy and legal categories, each with a source URL.

keyFindings.title: Era 1 (2006-2018): distillation as model compression
keyFindings.detail: Bucila, Caruana and Niculescu-Mizil showed in 2006 that a small network trained on the pseudo-labels of a large ensemble could match it; Hinton, Vinyals and Dean formalised soft-target 'dark knowledge' in 2015 and FitNets, sequence-level KD (Kim and Rush) and Born-Again Networks extended it to deeper students, seq2seq models and self-distillation. The technique was framed as deployment engineering, not competition.

keyFindings.title: Era 2 (2019-2022): the transformer compression wave
keyFindings.detail: DistilBERT and TinyBERT made distillation the standard recipe for shipping BERT-class models to production, cutting parameters by 40-90% while keeping most accuracy. Hugging Face's DistilBERT became one of the most downloaded models on the Hub and normalised distilled checkpoints as first-class open artifacts.

keyFindings.title: Era 3 (2023-2024): black-box distillation from frontier APIs
keyFindings.detail: Stanford Alpaca (52K text-davinci-003 demonstrations for under $600), Orca (GPT-4 explanation traces) and Distilling Step-by-Step showed that a small open model could inherit behaviour from a closed API using only outputs, not logits. MiniLLM and GKD reframed the loss for generative students (reverse KL, on-policy sampling). Frontier labs responded by hiding chain-of-thought (o1, September 2024) and by selling distillation themselves (OpenAI Model Distillation, October 2024; Bedrock, December 2024).

keyFindings.title: Era 4 (2025): reasoning distillation and the DeepSeek shock
keyFindings.detail: DeepSeek-R1 (20 January 2025) shipped six distilled dense students from 1.5B to 70B and proved that reasoning traces transfer cheaply; Sky-T1 ($450), s1 (1,000 examples), LIMO (817 examples) and OpenThoughts pushed the data floor lower. Nvidia lost nearly $600B of market value in one session, and within 48 hours OpenAI and the White House alleged DeepSeek had distilled OpenAI outputs. Gemma 3, Llama 4 and Qwen3 all disclosed teacher-student training as core recipe.

keyFindings.title: Era 5 (2026): adversarial distillation becomes statecraft
keyFindings.detail: Anthropic disclosed 16M+ Claude exchanges from ~24,000 fraudulent accounts tied to DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax (23 February 2026) and later a 28.8M-exchange campaign attributed to Alibaba's Qwen lab. OpenAI briefed Congress (12 February), OSTP issued a National Security and Technology Memorandum on adversarial distillation (23 April), the House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced H.R. 8283 43-0, the White House publicly accused Moonshot of distilling Anthropic's Fable for Kimi K3 (22 July), and senators introduced the BLADE Act (5 August). At the same time, on-policy distillation became the mainstream post-training recipe (Qwen3, DeepSeek-V4, Nemotron 3, Cursor).

keyFindings.title: The legal status of distillation is still unsettled
keyFindings.detail: As of September 2026 no court has ruled on whether API-output distillation is unlawful; the disputes rest on terms-of-service breaches, fraud (fake accounts, proxies) and export-control policy rather than copyright or patent. Bills such as H.R. 8283 explicitly preserve 'legitimate' distillation and rely on public attacker lists, sanctions and export controls instead of new IP rights.

timeline.title: Bucila, Caruana and Niculescu-Mizil publish 'Model Compression' at KDD 2006
timeline.detail: The paper shows that a single small neural network trained on unlabeled data pseudo-labeled by a large ensemble can match the ensemble's accuracy at a fraction of the size. It is the earliest widely cited ancestor of modern knowledge distillation.

timeline.title: FitNets introduces hint-based distillation into intermediate layers
timeline.detail: Romero et al. train thin, deep students by matching the teacher's intermediate representations ('hints') rather than only its outputs, establishing feature-based distillation.

timeline.title: Hinton, Vinyals and Dean post 'Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network'
timeline.detail: The paper coins 'distillation', introduces temperature-scaled soft targets and shows ensemble knowledge can be compressed into one model on MNIST and speech. It becomes the canonical citation for the field.

timeline.title: Kim and Rush propose sequence-level knowledge distillation
timeline.detail: Sequence-level KD trains a student on the teacher's beam-search outputs instead of per-token distributions, enabling small neural machine translation models. This is the direct ancestor of training on generated reasoning traces.

timeline.title: Born-Again Neural Networks show self-distillation improves students of equal size
timeline.detail: Furlanello et al. find that a student distilled from an identically sized teacher can outperform it, complicating the compression-only view of distillation.

timeline.title: TinyBERT distills BERT with transformer-layer and attention matching
timeline.detail: Huawei researchers combine general and task-specific distillation to build a 4-layer BERT that retains most of BERT-base accuracy at 7.5x fewer parameters.

timeline.title: Hugging Face releases DistilBERT
timeline.detail: DistilBERT is 40% smaller and 60% faster than BERT-base while retaining about 97% of its language-understanding performance. It makes distilled checkpoints a mainstream open-source artifact.

timeline.title: Stanford Alpaca fine-tunes LLaMA 7B on 52K text-davinci-003 demonstrations
timeline.detail: Data generation cost under $500 via the OpenAI API and fine-tuning under $100. Alpaca popularises black-box distillation from a proprietary API and prompts OpenAI's terms-of-service clause against training competing models to receive wide attention.

timeline.title: Google's 'Distilling Step-by-Step' uses LLM rationales as extra supervision
timeline.detail: Hsieh et al. train small task-specific models on chain-of-thought rationales extracted from a large model, outperforming standard fine-tuning with less data.

timeline.title: Microsoft's Orca learns from GPT-4 explanation traces
timeline.detail: A 13B model trained on step-by-step explanation traces from GPT-4 approaches ChatGPT on several benchmarks, showing that imitation of reasoning, not just answers, transfers capability.

timeline.title: MiniLLM proposes reverse-KL distillation for generative language models
timeline.detail: Gu et al. argue forward KL is ill-suited to open-ended generation and train students with reverse KL on their own samples, improving over standard sequence-level KD.

timeline.title: Generalized Knowledge Distillation (GKD) introduces on-policy distillation
timeline.detail: Agarwal et al. (Google DeepMind) train the student on its own generated sequences with teacher feedback, fixing train-inference distribution mismatch. On-policy distillation becomes the dominant recipe by 2025-2026.

timeline.title: Google releases Gemma; the 2B model is distilled from 7B
timeline.detail: Gemma's first generation establishes teacher-student training inside Google's open-model line, a pattern that continues through Gemma 2, 3 and 4.

timeline.title: Anthropic announces the Claude 3 family including Claude 3 Haiku
timeline.detail: Haiku is positioned as the fastest, cheapest tier of a three-tier lineup, cementing the industry pattern of a small model priced far below its flagship sibling.

timeline.title: Google says Gemini 1.5 Flash was trained by distillation from 1.5 Pro
timeline.detail: At I/O 2024 Google explicitly describes Flash as distilled from Pro, the first time a frontier lab named distillation as the recipe for its flagship low-cost tier. Launch pricing was $0.35 per million input tokens.

timeline.title: Gemma 2: 9B distilled from 27B, 2B from an unreleased 7B teacher
timeline.detail: Google scales distillation into Gemma 2, training smaller models on soft targets from larger ones instead of next-token prediction alone.

timeline.title: OpenAI launches GPT-4o mini at $0.15/$0.60 per million tokens
timeline.detail: GPT-4o mini undercuts Claude 3 Haiku ($0.25/$1.25) and Gemini 1.5 Flash ($0.35/$0.70) and becomes the default student model for OpenAI's later distillation API.

timeline.title: Nvidia's Minitron: compact models via pruning plus distillation
timeline.detail: Muralidharan et al. prune Nemotron-4 15B and retrain with distillation using up to 40x fewer tokens per model, reporting 1.8x compute savings for a model family.

timeline.title: Llama-3.1-Minitron 4B: 'LLM Pruning and Distillation in Practice'
timeline.detail: Nvidia applies the Minitron recipe to Llama 3.1 8B and Mistral NeMo 12B, retraining pruned models with 94B tokens of distillation. The models are released on Hugging Face for commercial use.

timeline.title: OpenAI releases o1-preview with a hidden chain of thought
timeline.detail: OpenAI forbids attempts to reveal o1's reasoning and cites competitive advantage alongside safety. Hiding traces is widely read as a defence against reasoning distillation.

timeline.title: Meta's Llama 3.2 1B and 3B built by pruning 8B and distilling from 8B/70B logits
timeline.detail: Meta states it used single-shot structured pruning from Llama 3.1 8B and incorporated logits from the 8B and 70B models as token-level targets during pre-training.

timeline.title: OpenAI launches Model Distillation in the API at DevDay
timeline.detail: Stored Completions, Evals and fine-tuning are combined into a workflow for distilling GPT-4o or o1-preview outputs into GPT-4o mini. OpenAI offered 2M free daily training tokens on GPT-4o mini through 31 October 2024.

timeline.title: Anthropic releases Claude 3.5 Haiku
timeline.detail: The small tier is refreshed alongside the upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet and the computer-use beta.

timeline.title: DeepSeek previews R1-Lite, its first reasoning model
timeline.detail: DeepSeek-R1-Lite-Preview shows visible chain-of-thought two months before the full R1 and its distilled family.

timeline.title: Amazon Bedrock Model Distillation enters preview
timeline.detail: AWS automates teacher generation, data synthesis and student fine-tuning within the same model family (Anthropic, Meta Llama, Amazon Nova), claiming up to 5x faster and 75% cheaper models with under 2% accuracy loss on RAG tasks.

timeline.title: Microsoft Phi-4 technical report: a 14B model that surpasses its teacher on STEM QA
timeline.detail: Phi-4 leans on synthetic data generated with GPT-4-class models, and Microsoft reports it exceeds the teacher on STEM question answering, a milestone for 'weak-to-strong' distillation.

timeline.title: DeepSeek-V3 released: 671B MoE trained in 2.788M H800 GPU-hours
timeline.detail: The technical report (arXiv 27 December) discloses the full training budget, roughly $5.6M at assumed rental prices, which seeds the January 2025 market narrative about cheap frontier models.

timeline.title: Sky-T1-32B-Preview: an o1-class reasoner trained for $450
timeline.detail: UC Berkeley's NovaSky team fine-tunes Qwen2.5-32B on 17K traces from QwQ-32B-Preview, reaching 43.3% on AIME 2024 and 82.4% on MATH500.

timeline.title: BIS publishes the Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion
timeline.detail: The Biden-era interim final rule creates a three-tier country system for advanced chips and, for the first time, controls exports of closed frontier model weights. Compliance was set for 15 May 2025.

timeline.title: DeepSeek-R1 released with six openly distilled students (1.5B to 70B)
timeline.detail: Alongside R1 and R1-Zero, DeepSeek publishes dense models distilled from R1 onto Qwen 2.5 and Llama 3 bases under an MIT licence. The paper reports the distilled students beat RL-from-scratch at the same size.

timeline.title: DeepSeek shock: Nvidia loses nearly $600B in market value in one day
timeline.detail: Nvidia falls about 17% and the Nasdaq about 3% as investors reprice AI capex on the belief that cheap distilled and open models reduce demand for frontier compute.

timeline.title: Microsoft and OpenAI probe DeepSeek-linked API data exfiltration
timeline.detail: Bloomberg reports Microsoft security researchers observed individuals believed linked to DeepSeek pulling large volumes of output through OpenAI's API in autumn 2024.

timeline.title: OpenThoughts project launches with a 114K-example open reasoning dataset
timeline.detail: The Bespoke Labs/Stanford/Berkeley collaboration scales up Bespoke-Stratos and releases OpenThinker-7B, aiming to open-source the reasoning-distillation data recipe.

timeline.title: OpenAI says it has evidence DeepSeek distilled its models; David Sacks cites 'substantial evidence'
timeline.detail: OpenAI tells the Financial Times it saw signs of distillation by DeepSeek in violation of its terms; White House AI adviser David Sacks repeats the claim on television. It is the first public accusation of adversarial distillation between frontier labs.

timeline.title: Gemini 2.0 Flash reaches general availability
timeline.detail: Google's second-generation Flash tier becomes the default Gemini model, continuing the distilled-flagship pricing strategy introduced with 1.5 Flash.

timeline.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling distills 1,000 Gemini Thinking traces
timeline.detail: Muennighoff et al. fine-tune Qwen2.5-32B on the s1K set (traces from Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking) and add 'budget forcing', exceeding o1-preview on competition math.

timeline.title: LIMO: 817 curated examples yield 63.3% on AIME24
timeline.detail: Ye et al. argue reasoning is elicited rather than taught, reaching 95.6% on MATH500 with about 1% of the data used by prior distillation recipes.

timeline.title: Apple publishes 'Distillation Scaling Laws'
timeline.detail: Busbridge et al. fit a scaling law for student performance as a function of teacher and student compute, giving compute-optimal distillation recipes for when a teacher exists and when it must be trained.

timeline.title: Nvidia reports record $39.3B quarter one month after the DeepSeek sell-off
timeline.detail: Q4 FY2025 revenue rose 78% year on year and data-center revenue hit $35.6B; CEO Jensen Huang argues reasoning models add a new scaling law for compute.

timeline.title: Gemma 3: all sizes (1B to 27B) trained with knowledge distillation
timeline.detail: Google DeepMind's technical report states every Gemma 3 model is distilled; Gemma3-4B-IT is reported competitive with Gemma2-27B-IT.

timeline.title: OpenAI's AI Action Plan submission calls DeepSeek 'state-controlled' and urges bans
timeline.detail: In its OSTP response OpenAI recommends barring 'PRC-produced' models in Tier 1 countries, citing IP-theft risk after its distillation allegations.

timeline.title: Meta's Llama 4 Maverick is codistilled from the 2T-parameter Behemoth
timeline.detail: Meta describes a novel distillation loss that dynamically weights soft and hard targets, run during Behemoth's own pre-training to amortise cost. Behemoth itself was never released.

timeline.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash released
timeline.detail: Google's first Flash model with configurable thinking budgets ships two months after 2.5 Pro.

timeline.title: Qwen3 launches with 'strong-to-weak' distillation for models from 0.6B to 14B
timeline.detail: Alibaba distills its 235B-A22B and 32B flagships into smaller students using off-policy then on-policy distillation, reporting better results than RL at roughly one-tenth the GPU hours.

timeline.title: Phi-4-reasoning distills o3-mini reasoning traces into a 14B model
timeline.detail: Microsoft fine-tunes Phi-4 on curated 'teachable' prompts with demonstrations generated by OpenAI's o3-mini.

timeline.title: Amazon Bedrock Model Distillation reaches general availability
timeline.detail: GA adds Nova Premier/Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 and Llama 3.3/3.2 pairings plus function-calling data augmentation for agent use cases.

timeline.title: Commerce rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule two days before its compliance date
timeline.detail: BIS says the tiered framework would have stifled US innovation and burdened allies; it issues separate guidance warning that using US chips to train Chinese models risks enforcement.

timeline.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4
timeline.detail: The Claude 4 generation resets the tiering that later distilled-tier releases (Haiku 4.5) are benchmarked against.

timeline.title: OpenThoughts3: 1.2M-example distillation dataset from QwQ-32B
timeline.detail: OpenThinker3-7B scores 53% on AIME 2025 and 54% on GPQA Diamond, beating DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B by 15-20 points via data-recipe ablations alone.

timeline.title: EU AI Office publishes the final General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
timeline.detail: Three chapters (transparency, copyright, safety and security) give GPAI providers a voluntary path to compliance ahead of the 2 August obligations.

timeline.title: White House releases America's AI Action Plan
timeline.detail: Ninety-plus actions across innovation, infrastructure and international security; its IP-protection language is later cited as the basis for anti-distillation legislation.

timeline.title: EU AI Act obligations for general-purpose AI models begin to apply
timeline.detail: New GPAI models placed on the EU market must meet transparency and copyright duties; Commission enforcement powers start 2 August 2026 and legacy models have until 2027.

timeline.title: Claude Opus 4.1 released
timeline.detail: An incremental flagship update that precedes Anthropic's autumn 4.5 lineup.

timeline.title: OpenAI launches the GPT-5 family: GPT-5, GPT-5 mini ($0.25/$2) and GPT-5 nano ($0.05/$0.40)
timeline.detail: Mini and nano tiers are priced 5x and 25x below GPT-5, extending the three-tier flagship/distilled pattern to OpenAI's fifth generation.

timeline.title: DeepSeek V3.1 adds hybrid thinking and non-thinking modes
timeline.detail: DeepSeek merges its chat and reasoning lines into one model, mirroring Qwen3's design.

timeline.title: Anthropic bars companies majority-owned by Chinese entities, citing distillation risk
timeline.detail: The policy blocks any entity more than 50% owned by companies headquartered in unsupported regions such as China, explicitly naming distillation as a way adversaries could advance their own models. Press coverage followed on 5 September.

timeline.title: Claude Sonnet 4.5 released
timeline.detail: Anthropic's mid-tier model becomes the reference point for Haiku 4.5's cost-performance claims two weeks later.

timeline.title: Claude Haiku 4.5: Sonnet 4-level coding at one-third the cost
timeline.detail: Priced at $1/$5 per million tokens, Haiku 4.5 is marketed as matching Sonnet 4 on coding at more than twice the speed, the clearest small-tier value claim of 2025.

timeline.title: Thinking Machines: on-policy distillation reaches RL parity at 50-100x less compute
timeline.detail: Kevin Lu and colleagues report 7-10x fewer gradient steps than RL and cite Qwen's 1,800 vs 17,920 GPU-hour comparison on AIME'24, attributing the gain to dense per-token reward.

timeline.title: Google launches Gemini 3 Pro and Deep Think
timeline.detail: Gemini 3 Pro debuts at 1501 Elo on LMArena and 91.9% GPQA Diamond; it becomes the teacher for the 3 Flash tier released a month later.

timeline.title: Claude Opus 4.5 released
timeline.detail: Anthropic closes 2025 with its fourth flagship refresh of the year.

timeline.title: DeepSeek V3.2 released with DeepSeek Sparse Attention
timeline.detail: The last V3-line model before V4; it follows the V3.2-Exp preview of 29 September.

timeline.title: Gemini 3 Flash released
timeline.detail: Google ships the small tier of its third generation one month after 3 Pro.

timeline.title: Apple and Google announce a multi-year Gemini partnership for Apple Foundation Models
timeline.detail: Bloomberg had reported a roughly $1B-per-year deal for a custom 1.2T-parameter Gemini; Apple later says its own models are refined using outputs from Gemini frontier models, a sanctioned, paid form of distillation.

timeline.title: Claude Opus 4.6 released
timeline.detail: First of Anthropic's 2026 releases; MiniMax markets M2.5 the same month as 1/20th the cost of Opus 4.6.

timeline.title: OpenAI memo to the House Select Committee on the CCP accuses DeepSeek of ongoing distillation
timeline.detail: OpenAI says DeepSeek-linked accounts built code to programmatically harvest outputs, used obfuscated third-party routers and unauthorized resellers, and were still distilling ahead of a new model launch.

timeline.title: Claude Sonnet 4.6 released
timeline.detail: Mid-tier refresh that lands one week before Anthropic's distillation-attack disclosure.

timeline.title: Anthropic discloses industrial-scale distillation attacks by DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax
timeline.detail: About 24,000 fraudulent accounts generated over 16 million exchanges: MiniMax 13M+ (agentic coding), Moonshot 3.4M+ (agentic reasoning, computer use), DeepSeek 150K+ (reasoning and reward-model data). Anthropic announces classifiers, behavioral fingerprinting and indicator-sharing with other labs.

timeline.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.5-Plus
timeline.detail: The generation immediately preceding the April-June campaign Anthropic later attributes to Qwen-linked operators.

timeline.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.4; mini and nano follow on 17 March
timeline.detail: GPT-5.4 mini goes to free-tier users while nano stays API-only, with prices above the original GPT-5 small tiers.

timeline.title: AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2026 (H.R. 8094) introduced
timeline.detail: Rep. Don Beyer's bill would require disclosure of training data and methods for foundation models, indirectly touching teacher-student provenance.

timeline.title: Google releases Gemma 4, again trained with distillation from a large instruction-tuned teacher
timeline.detail: Hugging Face's mid-2026 survey lists Gemma 4 among frontier open models using an improved teacher-student recipe.

timeline.title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act (H.R. 8283) introduced by Rep. Huizenga
timeline.detail: The bill creates a public 'AI Model Extraction Attackers List', discretionary sanctions and a Commerce/State information-sharing channel, while stating that legitimate distillation remains a valuable research tool.

timeline.title: House Select Committee hearing: 'China's Illicit Campaign to Steal and Subvert American AI'
timeline.detail: Witness testimony describes coordinated distillation campaigns using proxy accounts and jailbreaks against US frontier models.

timeline.title: House Foreign Affairs Committee reports H.R. 8283 favorably, 43-0
timeline.detail: The unanimous markup one week after introduction signals bipartisan consensus on treating adversarial distillation as a sanctionable act.

timeline.title: OSTP issues a National Security and Technology Memorandum on adversarial distillation
timeline.detail: Director Michael Kratsios says foreign entities, principally in China, run 'deliberate, industrial-scale campaigns' using tens of thousands of proxies; agencies are told to share intelligence, co-develop defences and explore accountability measures.

timeline.title: DeepSeek previews V4-Flash (284B) and V4-Pro (1.6T), trained with on-policy distillation from domain experts
timeline.detail: Per Hugging Face's survey, each domain (math, code, agents) gets an RL-trained specialist teacher and the unified model is trained with reverse-KL against them.

timeline.title: State Department cables posts and issues a demarche to Beijing over distillation
timeline.detail: Lawfare reports diplomatic posts were instructed to raise distillation attacks with host governments alongside a formal protest to China.

timeline.title: Claude Opus 4.8 released
timeline.detail: Last Opus 4.x release before the Claude 5 generation; falls inside the window of the alleged Qwen-linked extraction campaign.

timeline.title: CNAS publishes 'Adversarial Distillation' report
timeline.detail: Remler and Hayum estimate the 16M Claude exchanges could represent 150-400 billion extracted tokens and map a six-actor supply chain including token mixers and transfer stations.

timeline.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
timeline.detail: Fable 5 is the model the White House later says Moonshot distilled for Kimi K3; Mythos 5 is limited-access.

timeline.title: Anthropic tells the Senate Banking Committee of a 28.8M-exchange campaign it links to Alibaba's Qwen lab
timeline.detail: About 25,000 fraudulent accounts queried Claude between 22 April and 5 June 2026, targeting software engineering, agentic reasoning and cybersecurity; Anthropic calls it the largest known distillation attack on a commercial model. The letter became public on 24 June.

timeline.title: Apple says WWDC 2026 foundation models are refined using outputs from Gemini frontier models
timeline.detail: Craig Federighi describes Apple's third-generation models as trained on proprietary data and refined with Gemini outputs under the January partnership, an openly licensed instance of the same technique at the centre of the enforcement fights.

timeline.title: MiniMax launches M3 'frontier coding' model
timeline.detail: Four months after Anthropic's report, MiniMax ships a 1M-context multimodal coding model; MiniMax did not publicly rebut the distillation findings.

timeline.title: Claude Sonnet 5 released
timeline.detail: Anthropic's mid-tier joins the Claude 5 generation.

timeline.title: Hugging Face survey: distillation is now inside nearly every 2026 frontier release
timeline.detail: The post catalogues Gemma 4, DeepSeek-V4, MiMo-V2-Flash (multi-teacher on-policy distillation), GLM-5 (checkpoint-as-teacher), Nvidia Nemotron 3 Ultra (10+ domain teachers), Qwen3 and Cursor Composer 2.5 (self-distillation).

timeline.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3, a 2.8T-parameter open model
timeline.detail: Positioned as a frontier rival to US models; within a week the White House alleges it was built by distilling Anthropic's Fable.

timeline.title: White House accuses Moonshot of distilling Anthropic's Fable for Kimi K3; Treasury says sanctions are 'on the table'
timeline.detail: OSTP director Kratsios says Moonshot built a platform that switched access methods to evade detection and also alleges use of prohibited Nvidia GB300 servers via Thailand; Treasury Secretary Bessent warns of sanctions and Entity List designations.

timeline.title: Claude Opus 5 released
timeline.detail: Anthropic's flagship of the Claude 5 generation.

timeline.title: NPR: allegations of distillation spark debate over whether it is even illegal
timeline.detail: Legal analysts note the disputes rest on terms of service and fraud rather than copyright; US officials estimate unauthorized distillation costs US labs up to $6B a year.

timeline.title: DeepSeek V4-Flash official release
timeline.detail: The 284B model exits preview; V4-Pro (1.6T) follows on 13 August.

timeline.title: Senators introduce the BLADE Act (S. 5252) to block large-scale adversarial distillation
timeline.detail: Hagerty, Scott, Kim and Cortez Masto's bipartisan bill directs the executive branch to publicly list foreign distillation actors and authorises Commerce export controls and Treasury sanctions against them.

timeline.title: DeepSeek V4-Pro (1.6T parameters) released
timeline.detail: DeepSeek's largest model to date completes the V4 rollout.

timeline.title: Anthropic explains how Claude's text watermark works
timeline.detail: Output watermarking is one of the provenance measures discussed as a way to detect when a competitor's training data contains a frontier model's generations.

timeline.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8, a 2.4T-parameter model
timeline.detail: Shipped roughly two months after Anthropic's Senate letter attributing a 28.8M-exchange campaign to Qwen-linked operators.

timeline.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1
timeline.detail: The latest frontier generation as of this dashboard's update date.

glossary.definition: Training a smaller 'student' model to reproduce the behaviour of a larger 'teacher', classically by matching the teacher's softened output probabilities (Hinton et al., 2015).
The 2006 precursor to KD in which a compact model is trained on unlabeled data pseudo-labeled by a large ensemble (Bucila, Caruana and Niculescu-Mizil).
The full probability distribution a teacher assigns over outputs; its relative probabilities on wrong classes carry information a hard label does not.
Training a student on whole sequences generated by the teacher rather than per-token distributions (Kim and Rush, 2016); the basis of fine-tuning on reasoning traces.
Distillation using only a teacher's text outputs obtained via an API, with no access to weights or logits (Alpaca, Orca, DeepSeek-R1 accusations).
The student generates its own samples and the teacher scores them token by token (GKD, 2023); reported to match RL at 50-100x lower compute in 2025.
A distillation loss that penalises the student for placing mass where the teacher does not; preferred for generative models (MiniLLM).
Removing layers or widths from a large model and recovering accuracy with distillation (Nvidia Minitron, Llama 3.2 1B/3B).
Unauthorised, large-scale extraction of a proprietary model's outputs through fraudulent accounts, proxies or jailbreaks for the purpose of training a competing model.
The public list of foreign entities engaged in distillation attacks proposed by H.R. 8283 and the BLADE Act, to be maintained with Commerce and Treasury for sanctions and export controls.
